los.text: Identify the parts of the developing gastrointestinal tract, and the processes by which this tract and associated structures develop and mature
los.html:
• Gut tube (week 4): head-to-tail and side-to-side folding pinch off part of the yolk sac.
    • Endoderm → epithelium and glands
    • splanchnic mesoderm → muscle, connective tissue, visceral peritoneum.
RegionArteryBecomesPain felt
ForegutCoeliac trunkOesophagus, stomach, duodenum to the major papilla, liver, gallbladder, pancreas (lung bud also arises here)Epigastrium
MidgutSMARest of duodenum, jejunum, ileum, caecum, appendix, ascending colon, proximal 2/3 transverse colonPeriumbilical
HindgutIMADistal 1/3 transverse colon, descending and sigmoid colon, rectum, upper anal canal; bladder and urethral epithelium (from the cloaca)Suprapubic

Foregut organs

Stomach
  • Rotates 90° clockwise around its long axis (left vagus ends up in front, right behind)
  • The dorsal border grows faster → greater curvature
  • Rotation creates the lesser sac.
DuodenumLumen blocks with cells then recanalises (weeks 8–10); failure = duodenal atresia ("double bubble", linked with Down syndrome).
LiverHepatic diverticulum (week 4) grows into the septum transversum; gallbladder and cystic duct bud off it; fetal liver makes blood.
Pancreas
  • Dorsal and ventral buds
  • The ventral bud (with the bile duct) swings round behind the duodenum to fuse (weeks 6–7) → uncinate process and part of the head.
  • Main duct = ventral duct + distal dorsal duct.
  • Annular pancreas if the ventral bud encircles the duodenum
  • Pancreas divisum if the ducts don't fuse.

Midgut

HerniationThe midgut grows too fast and herniates into the umbilical cord (week 6).
Rotation270° anticlockwise around the SMA (90° outside, 180° on return); returns by week 10; caecum then descends to the RIF.
MalrotationRisk of volvulus (bilious vomiting in a newborn), Ladd's bands.
OmphaloceleGut fails to return; covered by a membrane; other anomalies common. Gastroschisis: wall defect beside the umbilicus, no sac.
Meckel's diverticulum
  • Vitelline duct remnant
  • Rule of 2s (2% of people, 2 feet from the ileocaecal valve, 2 inches long, 2 tissue types: gastric and pancreatic).

Hindgut

Cloaca
  • Divided by the urorectal septum (weeks 4–7) into the urogenital sinus (front) and anorectal canal (back)
  • The anal membrane breaks down in week 8.
Pectinate line
  • Where hindgut endoderm meets ectoderm.
  • Above = IMA, portal drainage, visceral nerves (painless), internal iliac nodes.
  • Below = pudendal vessels and nerves (painful), superficial inguinal nodes.
DefectsHirschsprung's (neural crest fails to reach the distal colon), imperforate anus.

Mesenteries

Dorsal mesenteryGreater omentum, gastrosplenic and splenorenal ligaments, small bowel mesentery, mesocolons.
Ventral mesentery(foregut only)Lesser omentum, falciform ligament.
Secondarily retroperitonealDuodenum, ascending and descending colon fuse to the posterior wall.
